papers.title: Agricultural imports in a changing world for disease risk management through the application of international standards and their economic and food security implications
papers.authors: Gezani Piet Mabunda, Ndivho Nemukondeni, Letlhogonolo Selaledi
papers.abstract: The expansion of global trade has generated substantial economic and social benefits; however, it has also intensified the transboundary movement of pests, pathogens and invasive species. These biosecurity threats pose significant challenges to the international trade of animals and animal products, plants and plant products, while creating heightened risks for importing countries. This review aims to examine the role of agricultural imports in the introduction and spread of pests and diseases, assess the associated biosecurity risks and evaluate existing management and regulatory approaches. A comprehensive literature review was conducted using Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus and relevant grey literature to identify and synthesize studies addressing trade-related disease and pest introduction, risk assessment frameworks and the implementation of sanitary and phytosanitary measures. The findings indicate that effective enforcement of biosecurity and control measures is critical for preventing the entry and establishment of harmful organisms. papers.title: Intensive pine plantation management shapes infectious agent communities in the generalist rodent Apodemus sylvaticus, with consequences for zoonotic hazard
papers.authors: Aloïs Berard, Maxime Galan, Julien Pradel, Caroline Tatard, Guillaume Castel
papers.abstract: Land use change is widely recognized as a major driver of emerging zoonotic diseases. Yet, while forest plantations are expanding worldwide, their consequences on the circulation of infectious agents in wildlife remain poorly understood. We investigated how native pine plantations and broadleaved habitats shape rodent-associated infectious hazard in the generalist wood mouse (Apodemus sylvaticus), in southwestern France. Using a multi-season survey, we screened 424 wood mice for a broad range of infectious taxa and compared infection probability and infected-host abundance among pine plantation edges, broadleaved hedgerows embedded within pine plantations and broadleaved forests. Using a combination of linear mixed model and joint species distribution modelling, we tested whether infectious hazard differed between pine plantations and broadleaved forests, whether broadleaved hedgerows shifted these patterns towards those observed in broadleaved forests, and how these habitat-related patterns varied across seasons. We detected 22 potentially infectious taxa, including nine recognized zoonotic bacteria. Season strongly influenced infectious patterns, while habitat effects were taxa a

papers.title: Influence of Climate Change on Cotton Pests and Their Management
papers.authors: K. Haripriya, M. Saranya, C. Muthu Lakshmi Bavithra, T. Manoramya, Muthuraman Yuvaraj
papers.abstract: Climate change significantly influences the ecology and dynamics of insect pests in cotton cultivation. Rising temperatures accelerate insect metabolism, shorten life cycles, and enable the expansion of pest populations into new geographical regions. Elevated atmospheric https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 levels alter host plant physiology, leading to increased feeding by chewing pests such as bollworms and enhanced survival of phloem feeders like aphids and whiteflies. Temperature fluctuations affect pest distribution, phenology, and life parameters, often resulting in more frequent and severe outbreaks. However, extreme heat can also reduce pest survival in certain cases. These shifts pose challenges to cotton production and necessitate adaptive pest management approaches. Integrated Pest Management (IPM), incorporating Bt cotton refuge strategies, biological and cultural control, pesticide rotation, and climate-smart agricultural practices, offers a sustainable pathway to mitigate the impacts of climate change on cotton pests while ensuring crop productivity and resilience.

papers.title: Integrated Irrigation and Disease Management Strategies for Sustainable Wheat Production and Improved Plant Health and Grain Yield
papers.authors: Amir Khan Jamali, Zahir Muhammad Larik, Videsh Kumar, Um E Habiba, Amanullah Maree
papers.source: OpenAlex / Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
papers.abstract: Wheat production was expected to provide reliable grain quality and farmer income while using less water and facing climatic variability, soil degradation, disease development, and rising energy costs. This literature-based paper critically synthesized verified research on irrigation, plant disease management, irrigation–disease interactions, sustainability, digital agriculture, and the Pakistan/developing-economy context. It considered irrigation and plant health as related management areas rather than completely separate input decisions. The available evidence did not identify a universal irrigation technology or deficit percentage. Instead, it supported a context-specific approach that considered stored soil water and rainfall, protected important growth stages, managed canopy humidity and nitrogen, used resistant cultivars and clean seed, and applied surveillance, forecasting, and fungicides when justified. Global and China-focused studies reported that moderate deficit or optimized water-saving irrigation could improve water productivity, whereas severe water deficit commonly reduced yield. papers.title: Evaluation of poison baits and development of a containment trap for the management of terrestrial snails
papers.authors: Deep A Gawas, Abhaykumar S Bagde, Shailendra D Wale, Jagdish B Patil, Deepak S Potdar
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
papers.abstract: A field investigation was conducted during the Kharif 2025 season in a naturally infested soybean plot at Sadoli Khalsa, Kolhapur, Maharashtra, to evaluate the efficacy of different poison baits and develop a custom physical trap for the management of terrestrial snails. Seven treatments, consisting of 2.5% metaldehyde integrated with various attractants (beer, wheat bran, rice bran, fruit, cabbage) and yeast, were evaluated under both open field conditions and within a custom-engineered containment trap. In open baiting, the beer-infused formulation proved superior, recording the highest overall mean catch of 10.44 snails, followed closely by the wheat bran bait with 9.50 snails. To prevent environmental degradation of the baits, a cylindrical plastic trap (25 cm height, 16 cm base) featuring three soil-level entry ramps and a 6 cm deep basal reservoir was developed. Deploying the poison baits inside these physical enclosures catalyzed substantial interception surges across all treatments compared to exposed layouts. Satellite remote sensing complements UAV observations by enabling wide-area, repeated monitoring at low cost; however, its effectiveness is limited by background interference from red-yellow soil and seasonal broadleaf discoloration. This study evaluated the ability of multisource satellite time-series features to improve PWD detection under complex environmental conditions. RESULTS: temporal component were the most sensitive indicators. Red-edge, near-infrared and shortwave infrared features effectively reduced background interference. Although S1 features alone showed limited performance, incorporating temporal information improved their sensitivity. The integration of single-time, sparse-temporal and time-series features achieved an overall accuracy of 0.76. CONCLUSION: Satellite time-series features significantly improve PWD detection under complex interference conditions by capturing disease-related temporal dynamics. papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Applied Analysis & Computation
papers.abstract: Understanding the transmission mechanisms of Moso bamboo sooty mold disease and the vector preference behavior of its vector insect (bamboo aphid) is of great significance for developing cost-effective integrated pest management strategies. This study constructs a compartmental model that incorporates vector preference to describe the transmission dynamics of the disease between bamboo plants and bamboo aphids. Through rigorous mathematical derivation, an explicit expression for the basic reproduction number $\mathcal{R}_0$ of the disease is obtained. Global sensitivity analysis identified the key parameters that most significantly influence the dynamics of disease transmission. papers.title: Climate-driven shifts in lumpy skin disease risk across Iran: Insights from ensemble species distribution models
papers.authors: Seyed Erfan Momenpour, Masoumeh Moghbel, Soheil Ghaem Maghami, Kambiz Amjadigolpayegani
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify the environmental determinants influencing the distribution of lumpy skin disease and to predict changes in its spatial distribution risk and potential geographic range across Iran under future climate change scenarios using ensemble Species Distribution Models (SDMs). To this end, following data cleaning and quality control of 3654 disease occurrence records, a total of 2849 presence points recorded between 2013 and 2024 were retained for model development. The CTA, GAM, GBM, and RF algorithms were implemented within an ensemble modelling framework. The final ensemble model (EMca) achieved a True Skill Statistic (TSS) score of 0.85, an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.96, and a Boyce index of 0.96 during calibration. For the validation data, the corresponding scores were 0.66, 0.89, and 0.93, respectively. The model therefore demonstrated broadly consistent predictive performance across calibration and validation based on these three evaluation metrics. papers.title: Pesticide Resistance and Environmental Concerns Under Climate Change
papers.authors: Uswa Maryam, Akhtar Hameed, Rana Binyamin, Hira Akhtar
papers.abstract: Pesticide resistance has emerged as a major concern in modern agriculture, posing significant threats to crop productivity, ecosystem stability, and global food security. By altering the temperature, precipitation patterns and atmospheric composition, climate change is further exacerbating the problem of pesticides resistance by modifying the biology, behavior, mobility and degradation of pathogens, pests and weeds. Increasing temperature accelerates metabolism and reproduction, enhances detoxification and increases the geographical range of pests and plant pathogens. Changing trends in the precipitation and humidity concentrations create favorable conditions for disease outbreaks, often resulting in escalating use of pesticides and increased selection pressure for resistant populations. Concurrently, the changing https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CO 2 levels and other greenhouse gases influences plant physiology that can change the pest feeding habits and pathogen infectivity patterns. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Investigating the role of neuropeptides in plant parasitic nematodes
papers.authors: Matthew Sturrock
papers.abstract: Plant parasitic nematodes (PPNs) devastate agriculture on a global scale causing severe annual economic losses. Withdrawal of the chemical nematicides used to control PPNs, due to their harmful environmental effects, has led to a short fall in our ability to manage these pests. This thesis explores different methodologies available to probe neuropeptide gene function in economically important PPNs. A proof of concept study utilising transgenic Bacillus subtilis to deliver PPN neuropeptides in a tomato seedling invasion assay identified several neuropeptides which induce aberrant behaviours in Meloidogyne incognita and Globodera pallida conferring resistance to tomato seedlings. This thesis demonstrated Bacillus subtilis signal peptide optimisation using NLP-15b. NLP-15b showed a potent effect during initial studies conferring host resistance from Meloidogyne incognita and Globodera pallida invasion. The nlp-15 gene was chosen for further investigations using several available platforms. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Population growth, numerous factories, and many vehicles are the primary sources of environmental pollution and toxic elements in the industrial city of Arak, Iran. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. The Top Enrichment Factor (TEF) of toxic elements of nickel, chromium, lead, and copper was higher than other elements. The Potential Ecological Risk (PER) index showed high and very high risk for the elements. For all elements, the Hazard Index (HI) values were higher for children than for adults. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: The localization of prostate cancer by ultrasound remains limited by the lack of B-mode conspicuity and the confinement of clinically approved microbubbles (MBs) to the vasculature. This precludes differentiating viable tumor, necrotic tissue, and margin-associated disease. We investigated prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted lipid-shelled perfluorocarbon nanobubbles (PSMA-NBs) in an orthotopic rabbit model using a clinical contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) system. We implanted PSMA-positive PC3pip-GFP tumors into the prostates of immunosuppressed New Zealand White rabbits and performed transabdominal imaging with PSMA-NBs, MBs, and Plain-NBs using identical protocols. To address tumor heterogeneity and ultrasound boundary ambiguity, regions of interest were defined from baseline B-mode images and segmented into the tumor core, rim, and a peritumoral area. papers.source: OpenAlex / Progress in Electronics and Communication Engineering
papers.abstract: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. papers.title: Shedding Light on Blind Spots: Application of the Domesticated Animal Citizens Model on Agroecology–an Ethical Discussion
papers.authors: Melina Katikaridis, Helena Röcklinsberg
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Agricultural and Environmental Ethics
papers.abstract: Abstract Agroecology presents itself as a transformative alternative to industrial agriculture, grounded in principles of justice, participation, and the dismantling of structural inequalities. Yet despite the centrality of domesticated animals within agroecosystems, agroecology lacks a coherent ethical account of human–animal relations. Animal production is commonly justified through ecological usefulness, leaving unexamined the moral assumptions that underlie their integration into farming systems. This paper argues that the concept of domesticated animal citizens, developed by Donaldson and Kymlicka (2011), offers a compelling political-theoretical framework for illuminating these blind spots. The citizenship model challenges moral hierarchy, reframes domestication as a source of ongoing moral responsibility, and articulates animals’ capacity for dependent agency in shared political communities. Applying this framework to agroecology exposes conceptual tensions between agroecology’s normative commitments and its lack of concern for domesticated animals. papers.abstract: This 2026 Super El Nino is among the most extreme events of changing temperature in the ocean-atmosphere system in the modern satellite era. These Sea Surface Temperature (SST) anomalies were +2.4°C or more than the Oceanic Nino Index (ONI) threshold for Nino 3.4. At the same time, the recent emergence of generative models of artificial intelligence (GenAI) has transformed how climate crises on planets are mediated, perceived and coping mechanisms are dealt with in digital public spheres. papers.authors: Zhili Zhao, Qian Li, Rui Pu, Kangqian Zhang, Yumei Dong
papers.abstract: The leaf-mining insect Tuta absoluta is a highly destructive pest that deploys candidate effector proteins to modulate host defences; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying this manipulation remain poorly understood. In this study, we characterise TaCYPE1, a predicted secreted cyclophilin-like effector, and demonstrate its role in promoting insect virulence. Transient expression of TaCYPE1 in Nicotiana benthamiana suppresses pattern-triggered immunity (PTI), including INF1-induced cell death, reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst, and defence-related gene expression. Notably, this immune suppression occurs independently of the conserved peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase (PPIase) activity of TaCYPE1. Stable overexpression of TaCYPE1 in tomato increases host susceptibility and enhances larval feeding, confirming its virulence function in a crop host. Mechanistically, TaCYPE1 physically interacts with host glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins (GR-RBPs), including SlRBP1 in tomato and NbRBGA in N. benthamiana, the latter contributes positively to selected immune responses and anti-herbivore defence. papers.title: Bottom-up effects of aboveground biota, invasive species and drought on soil animal communities
papers.authors: Marco Ilardi
papers.abstract: Soil ecosystems are facing the threat of a growing human population and the consequent global changes. Soil food webs are being exposed to unprecedented levels of disturbance, with the potential to disrupt the regulating interactions between soil biota components, and the role these components play in maintaining the stability of terrestrial ecosystems. This thesis investigates the response of soil animal communities to disturbances, focusing on perturbations originating above-ground and exerting their primary impact on the resources entering the system, with reverberating effects throughout the soil decomposer food web (bottom-up perturbation). The perturbations were applied through experimental manipulations, in order to investigate the disturbance in a controlled manner and detect the effects on soil microarthropods and nematodes. Changes in their abundance, taxonomic assemblage and/or trophic response indicate the extent of the disturbance effect and the roles these animals play as regulators of the whole soil food web. papers.authors: L. H. Schmitt, Richard A. How, Celeste H. Wale, Gregory Cozens, Peter B. S. Spencer
papers.abstract: We integrate demography, morphology and genetics to assess the biology and population structure of the endemic Kimberley rock-rat (Zyzomys woodwardi), a habitat specialist of the monsoonal tropics. The species is confined to the extreme north-west of the continent and 16 adjacent islands that were part of the mainland during the last Pleistocene glaciation. Islands became isolated from ~6500 years before present (BP), with their current populations being considered relictual. This, together with habitat patchiness and sedentary behaviour, promotes marked genetic and morphological variation. Capture rates were high on islands. All populations show a strong preference for moist rocky gullies containing boulder substrates and vine forest floristics. Demographics show large seasonal variation in activity and movement, with breeding occurring throughout the year. There is no sexual dimorphism. Analyses of skull metrics showed clear evidence of dwarfism in island populations, contrary to gigantism commonly observed in murids. papers.title: Transforming the rice–wheat system in India for climate resilience, resource-use efficiency, and food security
papers.authors: Sudhanshu Singh, VIRENDAR KUMAR, Ashish Kumar Srivastava, Eazhilkrishna Narayanasamy, Sunil Kumar
papers.abstract: The rice–wheat cropping system (RWCS) of the Indo-Gangetic Plains is fundamental to India’s food and nutritional security, accounting for a substantial share of national rice and wheat production while sustaining the livelihoods of millions of smallholder farmers. However, decades of intensive cultivation have led to groundwater depletion, soil degradation, declining factor productivity, residue burning, greenhouse gas emissions, and increasing climate vulnerability. This review synthesizes recent advances in technologies, management practices, and institutional innovations for the sustainable transformation of the RWCS. It examines the major biophysical, socio-economic, and policy constraints limiting system performance. The greatest gains in productivity, profitability, resource-use efficiency, and environmental performance arise from integrated production systems that combine improved genetics, conservation agriculture, precision resource management, mechanization, digital technologies, and supportive institutions and policies. papers.title: From waste to wealth: Production, properties, and emerging applications of agro-industrial biochar through the lens of TRL and trends
papers.authors: M. García-Rollán, M.C. Gutiérrez, Manuel Toledo, José Ángel Siles, A.F. Chica
papers.abstract: Agro-industrial waste represents one of the largest biomass waste streams worldwide. Its conventional management through open burning or landfill disposal causes environmental problems, including greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, soil degradation, and odor pollution. Sustainable valorization of these residues into value-added resources is therefore essential within a circular-economy framework. Among the available options, biochar production has gained significant attention because of its versatility, environmental potential, and compatibility with diverse residual feedstocks . This review examines the main thermochemical routes for carbon-material production, including slow, fast, and flash pyrolysis, hydrothermal carbonization, microwave-assisted pyrolysis, and torrefaction, and evaluates how feedstock composition and operating conditions determine product properties, process performance, and industrial feasibility. papers.abstract: Abstract Biomarkers contribute to measuring uptake in wildlife baiting applications, such as oral rabies vaccination (ORV), when marking capabilities are adequately validated. One biomarker, iophenoxic acid (IPA), can exist in multiple analogues and has the potential of being a quantitative marker for ORV uptake, but the marking capabilities of the different analogues have not been adequately validated for target species, such as raccoons ( Procyon lotor ). We experimentally fed captive raccoons 4 different encapsulated IPA analogues, methyl, ethyl, butyl, and pentyl, at 3 different doses, 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg, to evaluate marking and decay relative to dose. We then evaluated marking of 2 IPA analogues, ethyl and propyl, incorporated within the matrix of placebo ORV baits. We evaluated the concentration of each IPA analogue in raccoon serum using liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. For marking and decay evaluation, all 4 IPAs at all doses marked raccoons beyond 454 days, and we observed dose‐dependent relationships with serum IPA concentration. papers.authors: Babatunji Daramola, Xiaodan Pan, Jin‐Jia Yu, Changlu Wang
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Norway rats, Rattus norvegicus (Berkenhout), can carry ectoparasites of public health importance. However, this ectoparasite burden in residential complexes remains poorly characterized. This study examined ectoparasites recovered from Norway rats collected within New York City residential complexes and evaluated their associations with capture environment, host trait, and trap type. RESULTS: Six ectoparasite species were recovered. Spiny rat mites, Laelaps echidnina Berlese and Laelaps nuttalli Hirst, had the highest prevalence (56.1%), followed by the tropical rat mite, Ornithonyssus bacoti (Hirst) (40.3%), the spiny rat louse, Polyplax spinulosa (Burmeister) (39.5%), the Oriental rat flea, Xenopsylla cheopis (Rothschild) (38.4%), and the house mouse mite, Liponyssoides sanguineus (Hirst) (2.2%). Indoor-captured rats had higher abundance of X. cheopis, O. bacoti, and Laelaps spp., whereas P. spinulosa was more abundant on outdoor-captured rats. Cage-trapped rats (live rats) had higher counts of X. cheopis and Laelaps spp. than snap-trapped rats (dead rats). papers.authors: Samuel Omenka Ode, Nursakinah Suardi, Mohammed Ali Dheyab, Wesam Abdullah, Azlan Abdul Aziz
papers.abstract: Plant-based phytochemicals that operate as reducing and coordinating agents also create sustainable (green) frameworks for the construction of silver nanostructures (AgNPs). This review covers the inorganic and coordination chemistry underlying phytochemical-mediated AgNPs formation, with special emphasis on electron-transfer reduction, nucleation and growth kinetics, surface capping or ligand-exchange processes to control crystal facets, morphology, and zeta potential in detail. We systematically compare the specific functions of major secondary metabolites as either multifunctional reductants and stabilizing ligands (e.g., flavonoids, phenolic acids, terpenoids, alkaloids) or proteins or carbohydrates. In addition, we analyze how important reaction parameters (pH, temperature, precursor-to-extract ratios, incubation time, and solvent systems) modulate the size, shape, and colloidal stability of the nanostructures by means of speciation and binding equilibria. papers.authors: Ruonan Zhang, Jiali Huang, Xiaoping Fan, Wanqun Hu, Liang Dong
papers.abstract: Migraine is usually framed through trigeminovascular pathways and interactions among the brainstem, hypothalamus, and cortex. The cerebellum has received less attention, although human studies place it within circuits that process trigeminal nociception and vestibular signals. This narrative review examines anatomical and experimental work together with imaging, genetic, and clinical studies, giving greatest weight to direct human migraine evidence. Repeated-measures imaging suggests that cerebellar connectivity changes across the migraine cycle, but the cohorts are small. Structural findings vary with analytic method, and population based testing does not show a general cerebellar deficit in common migraine. papers.abstract: Commercial pastured and integrated poultry production (PIPP) represents an emerging area of poultry and crop production. As a “niche” area of commercial production, there is little overall knowledge about public opinion associated with PIPP. Here we utilized two complementary approaches to better understand current sentiment and associated challenges with PIPP-based production. Specifically, to understand farmer PIPP sentiment and challenges we surveyed commercial PIPP farmers. In parallel we captured stakeholder sentiment toward integrative farming (a slightly broader classification that includes PIPP) via the extraction of selected data (i.e., web-scraping) on the internet. The methodology combines web-scraping of various media and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to understand sentiment in a longitudinal fashion. Here we compared a farmer survey of 53 producers and 2,399 English language web-scraped online posts (e.g., from online forums, news sites, and blogs) from 1,089 unique authors between 2019 and 2021 to understand opinions of and experiences with PIPP. papers.authors: Sarmistha Rani Baruah
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Environmental and Agriculture Research
papers.abstract: The traditional Baree, or homestead-based production system, is an important component of rural landscapes in Assam. Often perceived simply as a household garden, Baree is in fact a multifunctional socio-ecological system where biodiversity, food production, livelihoods, traditional knowledge and human well-being are closely interconnected. A typical Baree may contain many plant species including fruit trees, vegetables, spices, medicinal plants, bamboo and other multipurpose species, together with birds, insects, soil organisms and other associated biodiversity. These components collectively provide food, income, ecosystem services and cultural benefits. This review examines the Baree from a socio-ecological perspective with a focus on its contributions to biodiversity conservation, food and nutritional security, livelihood diversification and human well-being. It also discusses emerging pressures such as commercialisation, land-use change, biodiversity loss, changing lifestyles, erosion of traditional knowledge and climate change. While aquatic species spatial use of mangroves and saltmarshes is well established, little is known about how terrestrial vertebrates use these habitats in Australia and under what contexts. Objectives We surveyed terrestrial vertebrates in mangroves and saltmarshes in a diversity of estuarine seascapes, scaling from areas with extensive nearby urbanisation to more natural areas, and quantified the relative influence of habitat structure and composition, and landscape configuration on assemblage structure. papers.abstract: Adaptive introgression, the transfer of beneficial alleles between species through hybridization, is increasingly recognized as an important source of adaptation to novel environments. However, the theory of adaptive introgression has primarily been developed for a single panmictic population, whereas many empirical examples involve spatially subdivided populations. In such systems, a low-frequency adaptive allele may either represent the leading edge of an adaptive travelling wave or occur in a subpopulation where the introgressed allele is locally selected against. We developed a simple prediction based on the relationship between adaptive allele frequency and introgressed tract length. Simulations predict a positive correlation during an ongoing sweep of an unconditionally beneficial allele, but no correlation under local adaptation. Tract erosion provides a recombination clock for time since introgression, which also determines the distance travelled by the adaptive wave and hence allele frequency in the former, whereas allele frequency is determined by local selection in the latter. papers.authors: Tahereh Zobeidi, Nadejda Komendantova
papers.abstract: Abstract Climate change poses an increasing threat to agricultural production and food security. While many European countries have developed National Adaptation Strategies (NASs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), the alignment between proposed policies and their supporting mechanisms remains under-explored. This study maps adaptation frameworks across ten European countries—Finland, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark, Estonia, Spain, Latvia, and Lithuania—to clarify diverse national policies and identify how specific instruments are prioritized to address adaptation goals. Drawing upon 20 official documents available on the Climate-ADAPT platform and using ATLAS.ti for qualitative analysis, 131 climate adaptation policies in agriculture were extracted to form a thematic synthesis. Then, we determined which policy instruments (categorized into four groups: information-based, legal and regulatory, economic, and infrastructural and physical instruments) were associated with each policy. papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Visual privacy‐sensitive objects in social images are often small, partially occluded, and unevenly represented in available training data, which limits the reliability of automatic privacy detection. This study develops a privacy‐sensitive object detection framework combining multi‐strategy image augmentation with SE‐Mask R‐CNN. Conventional photometric and geometric transformations are complemented by a DCGAN‐style generator to increase sample diversity, while SE modules are introduced into the ResNet50 backbone to recalibrate channel responses. A pseudo‐mask‐supervised branch is further incorporated to improve spatial localization of facial privacy regions. Experiments on the Human face subset of Open Images V6 show that GAN‐based augmentation reduces FID to 24.3 and increases SSIM to 0.92. The downstream detector trained with GAN‐augmented samples achieves an mAP of 78.90% and a recall of 82.50%. The complete SE‐Mask R‐CNN obtains an mAP of 0.88 and a small‐object AP of 0.79, compared with 0.72 and 0.58 for Faster R‐CNN and 0.81 and 0.68 for Mask R‐CNN, respectively.
